_comment: Public Turso configuration for the browser.
The only token here is readToken, scoped to `drops:data_read`. The
frontend reads the feed with it and can do nothing else — Turso enforces
the scope server-side, so the fact that the token ships in the bundle
There is deliberately no write token in this file. Publishing goes
through the Pages Functions, which hold a server-side token and the
master key needed to seal the destination URL; a browser cannot seal
anything, and a token with data_add/data_update/data_delete in a public
bundle would let anyone rewrite or delete the feed.
then create a new one and update this file, e.g.:
turso db tokens create lockdrop -p drops:data_read -e never
Note: there is no `data_write` action. A write scope has to be spelled
out as data_add / data_update / data_delete, and Turso rejects a token
then push the updated `public/turso.json` to Cloudflare Pages.
